summary.headline: Every sampled page -- homepage and every subject page -- delivers only 12 characters of visible text ('Khan Academy') to a non-JavaScript-executing fetcher, with no JSON-LD, no meta description and no noscript fallback — critical severity, Server-render or prerender the substantive page content (course/topic titles, descriptions, lesson structure) instead of shipping an empty shell plus a client-side data fetch; add JSON-LD (Organization at minimum, Course/LearningResource on subject and lesson pages) once real content is server-rendered.

findings.title: Every sampled page -- homepage and every subject page -- delivers only 12 characters of visible text ('Khan Academy') to a non-JavaScript-executing fetcher, with no JSON-LD, no meta description and no noscript fallback
findings.evidence: A plain fetch to https://www.khanacademy.org/, /math/algebra, /science/biology and /computing/computer-programming each returns HTTP 200, ~227KB, but reduces to 12 characters of visible text after stripping markup and scripts -- the page title, 'Khan Academy', and nothing else. There is no <noscript> element anywhere and no meta description. Zero JSON-LD blocks exist on any sampled page. Of the 227KB delivered, 223,634 bytes (over 98% of the page) is a single inline script assigning `__GROWTHBOOK_FEATURES__`, a feature-flag/experimentation configuration payload -- not course content. The only schema.org gesture present is `itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Organization"` on the `<html>` element itself, which carries zero `itemprop` attributes anywhere in the document -- a fully hollow declaration. This is not a bot-management challenge (no interstitial or soft-block signal fired, the response carries a correct canonical link and matching og:url for the requested path) -- it is a genuine, site-wide client-side-rendering architecture with no server-rendered or prerendered fallback of any kind for a non-executing client.

reproduction.observed: 12 (just the page title text) across all four sampled pages
reproduction.expected: Substantive course/lesson text -- titles, descriptions, topic lists -- present in the server-rendered response, the way a site of this scale and educational purpose needs to be readable by any assistant answering a question about a specific topic or lesson

suggested_action.summary: Server-render or prerender the substantive page content (course/topic titles, descriptions, lesson structure) instead of shipping an empty shell plus a client-side data fetch; add JSON-LD (Organization at minimum, Course/LearningResource on subject and lesson pages) once real content is server-rendered.
suggested_action.mechanism: An assistant that fetches a Khan Academy page today -- for any subject, at any depth -- receives no usable text regardless of how well-organized the underlying content actually is once JavaScript runs. This is the exact failure mode this skill exists to catch: a page that looks complete in a browser and is completely invisible to a non-executing fetcher. Because this is universal rather than isolated to one template, fixing the rendering path for even one representative page template (e.g. subject landing pages) would resolve the majority of the site's discoverability gap at once.
steps: Adopt server-side rendering or a prerendering layer for course/subject/lesson pages so the initial HTML response contains real page text.

Add JSON-LD once real server-rendered text exists: an Organization node with actual properties (the current microdata scope has none), and Course or LearningResource markup on subject and lesson pages.
Add a meta description per page stating what the page covers.
suggested_action.verification: A plain, non-JavaScript-executing fetch to a sample of pages (homepage, a subject page, a lesson page) returns substantive visible text matching what a browser shows.

opportunities.title: Populate the existing schema.org/Organization microdata scope, or replace it with JSON-LD, once server-rendered content exists
opportunities.rationale: The site already declares `itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Organization"` on the `<html>` element of every page -- someone already intended to carry Organization markup -- but it has zero `itemprop` attributes anywhere, so it currently asserts nothing. This is a smaller, more mechanical fix than the rendering gap itself and can happen independently of it.
opportunities.mechanism: A populated Organization node (name, url, logo, sameAs) gives assistants a minimal, reliable identity anchor for the entity even before the larger rendering fix lands.
steps: Add itemprop attributes (name, url, logo) to the existing microdata scope, or replace it with an equivalent JSON-LD Organization block.

not_assessed.check: Structured data completeness beyond the hollow Organization microdata, answerability, freshness/corroboration, and engagement (structured-data-audit, answerability-audit, freshness-corroboration-audit, engagement-audit)
not_assessed.reason: Every sampled page delivers no visible text to a non-JavaScript-executing fetcher (see the render-extractability finding). There is no prose to derive questions from, no dates or self-description sentences to check for freshness, and no above-the-fold content to assess for answer continuity -- all of these checks operate on text that, for this site, does not exist in the server response at all.
not_assessed.impact: This audit cannot say whether Khan Academy's actual lesson content (once rendered) is well-written, current, or well-corroborated -- only that no automated, non-JS-executing agent ever gets far enough to read it. This mirrors the wsj.com and airbnb.com reports' experience: a severe enough delivery-stage finding leaves nothing for later stages to evaluate, and that is reported honestly rather than guessed at.

not_assessed.reason: No headless-browser engine (Playwright/Puppeteer) was available in this run's environment, and this is exactly the kind of site where the distinction matters most, since all content loads after JavaScript execution.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot assess the actual on-site experience for a client that does execute JavaScript.
